sentences.en: You know, Jenna, you always say that Kendra would be like if you and I had a best friendship baby.

sentences.zh: 她既有安吉拉的趣味，又兼具我那种事事讲究电子表格的严谨。

sentences.en: You know, she wants to help you organize your life in the way that works best for you.
sentences.zh: 你知道，她想以最适合你的方式帮你打理生活。

sentences.zh: 但她同时也希望你在打理生活时能感到轻松愉快。

sentences.en: But the best person to tell you about The Lazy Genius is the Lazy Genius herself, Kendra Adachi.

sentences.en: And we're going to talk with her about some of our favorite Lazy Genius principles.
sentences.zh: 我们将和她聊聊我们最喜欢的一些“懒人天才”原则。

sentences.en: And Kendra is going to tell us where The Office characters fall on her scale of lazy to genius.
sentences.zh: 肯德拉还会告诉我们，《办公室》里的角色在她的“懒人到天才”量表上分别处于什么位置。

sentences.en: I cannot wait.

sentences.en: And the rest of The Office gang.

sentences.zh: 等我们回来，“懒人天才”本人肯德拉·阿达奇将加入我们，

sentences.zh: 但我看着你，心里想的就是：那是她的声音。

sentences.en: Well, you know, Kendra, we love your podcast, The Lazy Genius.
sentences.zh: 肯德拉，我们很喜欢你的播客《懒人天才》。

sentences.en: And we would love for you to tell our audience, what is a lazy genius?
sentences.zh: 我们很想请你告诉我们的听众，什么是“懒人天才”？

sentences.en: A lazy genius is someone who is a genius about the things that matter and lazy about the things
sentences.zh: “懒系天才”是指在重要的事情上精益求精，而在无关紧要的事情上

sentences.en: that don't.
sentences.zh: 选择偷懒的人。

sentences.en: So the thing that the problem is that there are a lot of voices that are telling us all
sentences.zh: 问题在于，有很多声音在告诉我们

sentences.en: the different things that should matter.
sentences.zh: 各种各样所谓“重要”的事情。

sentences.en: And we want to be like good rule followers and like decent people.
sentences.zh: 我们想做循规蹈矩的好人，做个像样的人。

sentences.en: And we're like, OK, well, this should matter.
sentences.zh: 于是我们想，好吧，这事儿应该很重要。

sentences.en: I'll work hard on this.
sentences.zh: 我要在这上面努力。

sentences.en: I'll do this thing.
sentences.zh: 我要把这事儿做好。

sentences.en: And then we just like end up with adrenal fatigue.
sentences.zh: 结果最后我们只会精疲力竭。

sentences.en: It's like a whole thing.
sentences.zh: 就是这么回事。

sentences.en: So I want to give people permission to choose what matters to them based on their own lives
sentences.zh: 所以我希望能让大家有底气去选择对自己真正重要的事，基于各自的生活、

sentences.en: and their own seasons of life and their personalities and their families and all of that.
sentences.zh: 人生阶段、性格、家庭等等因素。

sentences.en: And then put energy into things that matter to them.
sentences.zh: 然后把精力投入到那些对他们重要的事情上。

sentences.en: Like it's not that you have to like messy hair don't care your entire life away.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说你要一辈子都过着“头发乱糟糟，我才不在乎”的生活。

sentences.en: You can care about stuff.
sentences.zh: 你当然可以有所追求。

sentences.en: You can be good at stuff.
sentences.zh: 你当然可以把事情做好。

sentences.en: Like I think that's a wonderful thing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一件很棒的事情。

sentences.en: You want to be a genius at certain things in your life.
sentences.zh: 你当然希望在生活中某些方面成为天才。

sentences.en: But in order to do that, you also got to let some other stuff go.
sentences.zh: 但为了做到这一点，你也必须学会放下一些别的东西。

sentences.en: You got to be lazy about some stuff.
sentences.zh: 你得学会在某些事情上偷懒。

sentences.en: And I just give people principles to help do that in their own way.
sentences.zh: 我只是提供一些原则，帮助人们用自己的方式做到这一点。

sentences.en: And then also I have this podcast that kind of breaks it down topically to kind of help you be a
sentences.zh: 此外，我还有一个播客，按主题进行拆解，帮助你

sentences.en: lazy genius about whatever the thing is.
sentences.zh: 在任何事情上都能成为“懒系天才”。

sentences.en: And so I've been doing that for – I've been teaching people how to be a lazy genius since 2016.
sentences.zh: 我从2016年就开始教大家如何成为“懒系天才”了。

sentences.en: Well, Kendra, the very first podcast I heard of yours was called something like
sentences.zh: 肯德拉，我听的你的第一个播客标题大概是

sentences.en: How to Organize Paper in Your Home.
sentences.zh: 《如何整理家中的纸质文件》。

sentences.en: Oh, she talked about that so much, Kendra.
sentences.zh: 噢，肯德拉，她当时讲了好多关于那个的内容。

sentences.en: All the paper that comes in your home.
sentences.zh: 家里收到的所有纸质文件。

sentences.en: And this was my introduction to you.
sentences.zh: 那就是我认识你的开始。

sentences.en: I didn't really know what a lazy genius was yet.
sentences.zh: 当时我还不知道什么是“懒系天才”。

sentences.en: And so when I clicked on that podcast, I thought you were going to literally prescribe to me what to do with all the papers that come into my house,
sentences.zh: 所以当我点开那个播客时，我以为你会直接告诉我该怎么处理家里收到的所有纸张，

sentences.en: all of my kids' artwork, all of the school forms, all of the, you know, insurance follow-up from when you go to the doctor,
sentences.zh: 所有的孩子画作、学校表格，还有你看完医生后收到的那些保险单据，

sentences.en: all the things that accumulate in a pile or multiple piles.
sentences.zh: 所有堆成一堆或好几堆的东西。

sentences.en: And to my surprise, you did not tell me what to do with the paper.
sentences.zh: 令我惊讶的是，你并没有告诉我该怎么处理这些纸。

sentences.en: You asked me what mattered to me about these piles of paper.
sentences.zh: 你问我，这些成堆的纸里，什么对我来说才是重要的。

sentences.en: And it was such this light bulb for me because you're right.
sentences.zh: 那一刻我茅塞顿开，因为你说得对。

sentences.en: I watch Instagram and there's all these videos of like special frames that I can put my kids' artwork in.
sentences.zh: 我刷Instagram时，总能看到各种视频，推荐我买那种可以放孩子画作的特殊画框。

sentences.en: And I'm like, should I be doing that?
sentences.zh: 我心想，我是不是也该这么做？

sentences.en: Should I be buying the frames where I cycle the different paintings in and out?
sentences.zh: 我是不是该买那种可以轮换展示画作的画框？

sentences.en: I tried it.
sentences.zh: 我试过。

sentences.en: I never cycled a single thing.
sentences.zh: 但我从来没换过哪怕一张画。

sentences.en: And what I learned from your podcast, Kendra, was that a lot of that paper didn't matter to me.
sentences.zh: 肯德拉，从你的播客里我学到的是，很多纸质文件对我来说根本不重要。

sentences.en: And I could let it go.
sentences.zh: 我可以选择放下它们。

sentences.en: It was okay if we looked at a piece of the artwork and we appreciated it and then we let it go.
sentences.zh: 如果我们欣赏过孩子的画作，然后把它处理掉，这完全没问题。

sentences.en: And it was great.
sentences.zh: 那感觉棒极了。

sentences.en: It was very freeing because you helped me name what did matter to me about it.
sentences.zh: 这让我感到非常解脱，因为你帮我明确了什么对我来说才是重要的。

sentences.en: And then you helped me allow myself to be lazy about the other parts.
sentences.zh: 然后你又帮我学会了在其他方面允许自己偷懒。

sentences.en: And it was transformative.
sentences.zh: 这简直是脱胎换骨的改变。

sentences.en: It really was.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And it was so simple.
sentences.zh: 而且这一切竟如此简单。

sentences.en: But you do that on your podcast all the time.
sentences.zh: 但你在播客里经常这么做。

sentences.en: You did one about packing school lunches that changed my life.
sentences.zh: 你做过一期关于准备学校午餐的节目，那真的改变了我的生活。

sentences.en: I'm so glad.
sentences.zh: 我太高兴了。

sentences.en: And here's the thing that I think is so vital to this is your decision to go, we're going to look at this paper and go, yes, this was so lovely.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这其中最关键的一点是，你决定说：我们要看看这张纸，然后说，嗯，这真可爱。

sentences.en: Literally into the recycling it goes.
sentences.zh: 然后直接把它扔进回收箱。

sentences.en: You are just as, because we're talking about like in that context, kids' artwork.
sentences.zh: 你依然是，因为我们是在那种语境下讨论，比如孩子的艺术作品。

sentences.en: Like you're just as good of a mother as someone who cycles through the artwork.
sentences.zh: 你和那些把艺术作品循环利用的人一样，都是好妈妈。

sentences.en: Like we have this sort of, it's almost like a gas gauge, you know, of like we have to be all things.
sentences.zh: 我们好像有一种油量表，你知道吧，觉得我们必须面面俱到。

sentences.en: It's like a full tank.
sentences.zh: 就像油箱必须加满一样。

sentences.en: In order to be a full tank of this kind of person, you have to care this way.
sentences.zh: 为了成为那种“满油”的人，你必须以某种方式去在意。

sentences.en: And that's just not the way it goes.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: And so I just love that you're like, we're going to, we're going to look at this and go, remember this?
sentences.zh: 所以我很喜欢你这种做法，我们看看这个，然后说，还记得这个吗？

sentences.en: This was so fun.
sentences.zh: 当时真有趣。

sentences.en: But we don't have to keep it in order for that experience to matter.
sentences.zh: 但我们不需要为了让那段经历有意义而把它留下来。

sentences.en: So I'm so glad.
sentences.zh: 所以我太高兴了。

sentences.en: You're right.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: And that's what the entire show, all 300 something episodes at this point, it really does.
sentences.zh: 这正是整个节目，到目前为止三百多期节目的核心所在，确实如此。

sentences.en: I really want to help you see more than help you figure out what to do.
sentences.zh: 我更想帮你去“看见”，而不是帮你去想“怎么做”。

sentences.en: You have to see it your way first before you can do anything anyway.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，你必须先用自己的方式去看待，才能去做任何事。

sentences.en: So just try to set you up with like the right pair of glasses, you know?
sentences.zh: 所以我只是想帮你戴上一副合适的眼镜，你懂吗？

sentences.en: What I like about it too is that you let everyone approach it their way.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你的一点是，你让每个人都能用自己的方式去处理。

sentences.en: It's not, there's no one path to like, how do we save art?
sentences.zh: 并没有什么所谓的唯一途径，比如我们该怎么保存艺术品？

sentences.en: How do we appreciate our kids' art in that pile of paper?

sentences.en: Maybe it'll transform your life.
sentences.zh: 也许它会改变你的生活。

sentences.en: But Kendra, you also have a new episode out today.
sentences.zh: 不过肯德拉，你今天也发布了新的一期节目。

sentences.en: Hey, it's episode 351, and it's called How to Lazy Genius Your Whole Life, which is kind of the perfect episode if you're a new listener.
sentences.zh: 嘿，那是第351期，标题是《如何让你的整个人生都变得“懒人天才”》，如果你是新听众，这期节目简直完美。

sentences.en: Kendra, you said it's kind of a beginner's guide to the lazy genius, but also a good reminder of the whole reason you're doing this, which is, like you said earlier,
sentences.zh: 肯德拉，你说这算是“懒人天才”的入门指南，但也是对你做这件事初衷的一个很好的提醒，正如你之前所说，

sentences.en: you want to make this a lifestyle and a mindset and not just a random choice that we make every once in a while.
sentences.zh: 你想让这成为一种生活方式和思维模式，而不仅仅是我们偶尔做出的随机选择。

sentences.en: You also had a great episode last week called Starting Fresh When You Can't Start Over.
sentences.zh: 你上周还有一期很棒的节目，叫《无法重头开始时如何重新出发》。

sentences.en: It's all about the January pressure to change everything.
sentences.zh: 这期节目讲的是一月份人们想要改变一切的压力。

sentences.en: And your episode is so great because it really encourages people to start small.
sentences.zh: 你的节目非常棒，因为它真的鼓励人们从小事做起。

sentences.en: And that's one of the – there are 13 lazy genius principles that are in my first book that are basically the foundation of everything I talk about.
sentences.zh: 这是我的第一本书中提到的13个“懒人天才”原则之一，它们基本上是我所谈论的一切的基础。

sentences.en: And one of the principles is to start small.
sentences.zh: 其中一个原则就是从小事做起。

sentences.en: And it's the most annoying of all the 13.
sentences.zh: 而且它是这13个原则中最让人心烦的一个。

sentences.en: It's so annoying.
sentences.zh: 太让人心烦了。

sentences.en: Nobody wants to start small, including myself.
sentences.zh: 没人想从小事做起，包括我自己。

sentences.en: You don't see any progress right away.
sentences.zh: 你不会立刻看到任何进展。

sentences.en: It just feels like it's not really going to do anything.
sentences.zh: 感觉就像它真的起不到什么作用一样。

sentences.en: But honestly, those small steps over, like, even a long time,
sentences.zh: 但老实说，那些微小的进步，哪怕是经过很长一段时间，

sentences.en: those are the things that stick way more than these big systems that we build over three days in January that then fall apart.
sentences.zh: 比起我们在元月花三天时间建立、随后又分崩离析的宏大体系，这些微小的进步反而更能持久。

sentences.en: So, I do love that this is a good reminder of, like, hey, we're going to start small with this.
sentences.zh: 所以我很喜欢这一点，它很好地提醒了我们：嘿，我们要从小处着手。

sentences.en: And that is actually going to make it more doable and accessible and probably even work in a way that you want it to work, even though it's annoying.
sentences.zh: 这实际上会让事情变得更可行、更容易实现，甚至能以你想要的方式运作，尽管这过程可能很烦人。

sentences.en: Starting small is so annoying, but it really does help.
sentences.zh: 从小处着手真的很烦人，但它确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: So, yeah, I'm excited for you all to listen to that.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我很期待你们大家去听那一期。

sentences.en: Kendra, I have your sticker that says, start small, on my computer.
sentences.zh: 肯德拉，我的电脑上贴着你那张写着“从小处着手”的贴纸。

sentences.en: That's so fun.
sentences.zh: 那太有趣了。

sentences.en: And it's crazy because I lost my computer on a flight.
sentences.zh: 说来疯狂，因为我曾在一次飞行中弄丢了我的电脑。

sentences.en: I got off the airplane once and I left my computer on the plane.
sentences.zh: 有一次我下了飞机，把电脑落在了飞机上。

sentences.en: And I can't believe it, but Air Canada found it.
sentences.zh: 我简直不敢相信，但加拿大航空竟然找到了它。

sentences.en: It had flown to multiple other cities, but they managed to find it.
sentences.zh: 它当时已经飞往了其他好几个城市，但他们还是设法找到了它。

sentences.en: And when they asked me, how can you identify your computer?
sentences.zh: 当他们问我，你如何证明那是你的电脑时？

sentences.en: And I said, it has a sticker on it that says, start small.
sentences.zh: 我说，上面有一张贴纸，写着“从小处着手”。

sentences.en: And they said, we found it.
sentences.zh: 他们就说，我们找到了。

sentences.en: We found your computer.
sentences.zh: 我们找到你的电脑了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Oh, that's incredible.
sentences.zh: 噢，那真是太不可思议了。

sentences.en: And it was all because I was so committed to the lazy genius principle of starting small.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是因为我如此坚信“懒人天才”中“从小处着手”的原则。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And I love it.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这个原则了。

sentences.en: It's a good one for people who skew genius, who lean that way a lot and who are like, let's roll.
sentences.zh: 对于那些倾向于“天才”思维、习惯于那种模式、总想着“冲啊”的人来说，这非常适用。

sentences.en: Let's go.
sentences.zh: 行动起来。

sentences.en: Let's get it all done right now because we can run that direction until we fall down sad and crying.
sentences.zh: 让我们现在就把一切都搞定，因为我们确实可以那样拼命，直到最后精疲力竭、伤心落泪。

sentences.en: And so start small kind of helps us temper that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 所以“从小处着手”能帮我们稍微克制一下那种冲动。

sentences.en: It's like the kindest little break tap.
sentences.zh: 就像是一个最温柔的刹车踏板。

sentences.en: You know, it's like, hey, we're all right.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是说，嘿，我们没事的。

sentences.en: We're all right.
sentences.zh: 我们没事的。

sentences.en: Start small.
sentences.zh: 从小处着手吧。

sentences.en: Bringing it back to the podcast, that's really why I love this work that I do
sentences.zh: 回到播客的话题，这确实是我热爱这份工作的原因，

sentences.en: because the 13 principles and the way the lazy genius method, all of these things are
sentences.zh: 因为这13条原则以及“懒人天才”方法论，所有这些东西，

sentences.en: really versatile no matter how you operate, no matter how you think, no matter what your
sentences.zh: 无论你如何行事，无论你如何思考，无论你的生活看起来是什么样，

sentences.en: life looks like, no matter what season you're in.
sentences.zh: 无论你正处于人生的哪个阶段，它们都非常通用。

sentences.en: Like they really are tools for everyone because they're personal and versatile and they work.
sentences.zh: 它们确实是适合每个人的工具，因为它们个性化、通用且有效。

sentences.en: They are not like self-help steps that only work for a certain kind of person.
sentences.zh: 它们不像那些只对特定人群有效的自助步骤。

sentences.en: They're much broader and kinder than that.
sentences.zh: 它们比那更广泛、更友善。

sentences.en: So it's really fun work to do because it helps anybody who is interested in being helped
sentences.zh: 所以做这份工作真的很有趣，因为它能帮助任何想要获得帮助、

sentences.en: and wanting to see their life this way.
sentences.zh: 并希望以这种方式看待生活的人。

sentences.en: It really does help.
sentences.zh: 它确实很有帮助。

sentences.en: It really does work.
sentences.zh: 它确实行之有效。

sentences.en: So it's such a fun treat to be able to share that with the Office Ladies listeners.
sentences.zh: 所以能与《办公室女士》的听众们分享这些，真是一件乐事。

sentences.en: This is so fun.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: Well, you're so, so fantastic at it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你在这方面做得太棒了。

sentences.en: We're so thrilled to have you on Office Ladies and we can't wait for people to hear your episodes.
sentences.zh: 我们非常高兴你能来到《办公室女士》，我们迫不及待想让大家听到你的节目了。

sentences.en: Yeah, we are so excited for you to be joining the Office Ladies Network.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们非常兴奋你能加入《办公室女士》网络。

sentences.en: Yeah, we're a network.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们是一个网络。

sentences.en: We're a dang network, y'all.
sentences.zh: 我们可是个货真价实的网络，伙计们。

sentences.en: Now we are.
sentences.zh: 现在我们是了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I love it.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: Everybody, please go subscribe to the Lazy Genius.
sentences.zh: 各位，请一定要去订阅“懒人天才”。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你们猜怎么着？

sentences.en: You will hear us on Lazy Genius next week.
sentences.zh: 下周你们就能在“懒人天才”里听到我们了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We're going to be your gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我们将担任你们的嘉宾。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: Everybody's going to lose their minds.
sentences.zh: 大家一定会为此疯狂的。

sentences.en: It's so fun.
sentences.zh: 太有趣了。

sentences.en: It's so fun.
sentences.zh: 真的太有趣了。

sentences.en: Thank y'all so much for having me.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们邀请我。

sentences.zh: 感谢大家收听《办公室女士》。
